evidence: Traupman 409: what’s wrong with you?, quid est tibi? or quid est tēcum?
Plaut. Curc. 236: sed quid tibi est?

terms.comment: Literally “what of a matter is it?”. Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections in this form; Traupman is the only evidence.

phrases.english: “What’s the matter? Do your ears hurt?”

phrases.latin: quid agis? — Vīvō. — Nempe ut dignus es. sed quid tibi est?
phrases.english: How are you? — Alive. — As you deserve, no doubt. But what’s wrong with you?

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: pp. 92, 409, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026 and 9 November 2026.
